key_insight: CARS anchors attention to coronary centerlines to rapidly predict pressure and velocity across variable lumen geometries.
engineering_relevance: It enables coronary flow evaluation in 87 ms per case versus 572–1,063 s for CFD, with strong agreement on pressure-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR).
method: Inputs: image-derived centerline, per-point lumen radius, and scalar inlet flow rate.
Predicts steady incompressible flow pressure and velocity at arbitrary query points.
Uses centerline-anchored attention with O(N n_f) geometry-fusion cost rather than O(N²).
evidence_signal: Trained per territory on 2,700 OpenFOAM solutions with synthetic lesions, CARS achieved left/right test relative ℓ₂ errors of 0.120/0.063 for pressure and 0.149/0.119 for velocity, with 97.7%/96.3% agreement on the FFR ≤ 0.8 decision.
watch_item: Predicted velocity does not satisfy continuity closely enough for derived quantities, and model weights are territory-specific.
paper_title: CARS: a centerline-anchored attention surrogate for coronary blood flow on skeleton-generated lumen geometries
